audit_findings.title: The updated capital structure is paired with stale interest expense
audit_findings.magnitude: computed $55m annual coupon on the May 2026 notes; filed six-month 2026 interest expense of $345m was $49m above 2025, including $16m attributed to the expired swap
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 OE anchor retains interest based on the earlier financing structure, while June 2026 debt and shares capture subsequent debt-funded capital allocation.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, our total indebtedness, excluding the deduction for unamortized deferred financing costs and discount, was approximately $12.5 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated. The new $1.0bn notes alone add $55m of annual pre-tax interest, equal to 3.9% of the $1.425bn anchor, and the March 2026 hedge expiration adds another continuing burden. Capitalizing both effects could materially reduce value, although the exact after-tax normalization is not established.
audit_findings.action: Recalculate OE using the June 2026 debt schedule, contractual coupons, current unhedged term-loan rate, financing-cost amortization, hedge settlements and interest income; then rerun all scenarios with the June share count.

audit_findings.title: Recurring contract-acquisition investment is not visibly deducted
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $231m cash cost less $57m amortization equals a computed $174m gap, or 12.2% of anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: If omitted, recurring cash contract-acquisition spending is absent from OE while the resulting system growth is included in forecast growth.
audit_findings.evidence: We capitalize consideration paid to incentivize hotel owners to enter into management and franchise contracts with us as contract acquisition costs and the incremental costs to obtain the contracts as development commissions and other, both of which are generally fixed.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash expenditure and amortization difference are demonstrated, but omission from the supplied OE calculation is not. If the full 2025 gap is recurring and absent, applying the base operating-value-to-OE factor gives about $2.445bn, or $10.58 per share, of overstatement before considering maintenance-versus-growth classification.
audit_findings.action: Trace the OE calculation line by line, separate maintenance and growth contract spending, deduct the amount required to sustain each scenario, and rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may embed a temporary $465 million program deficit as permanent
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $465m 2025 deficit; computed as 32.6% of anchor OE and approximately $6.533bn or $28.28 per share under the base capitalization factor
audit_findings.mechanism: A recoverable reimbursement timing deficit retained in anchor OE would be projected as a permanent annual operating loss.
audit_findings.evidence: However, over the life of the operation of these programs, the expenses incurred related to the indirect reimbursements are designed to equal the revenues earned from the indirect reimbursements over time such that, in the long term, the programs will not earn a profit or generate a loss and do not impact our economics, either positively or negatively.
audit_findings.explanation: The $465m accounting deficit and contractual recovery rights are demonstrated; whether OE already removed the deficit is unresolved. If retained and fully recoverable, its capitalization would materially increase value. The contractual language does not by itself prove the full amount or timing of recovery.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the OE anchor to the reimbursement adjustment, associated receivables, deferred revenue and loyalty liabilities; establish enforceable recovery and timing, then rerun with only the economically recoverable normalization.

audit_findings.title: The entire cash balance may not be distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum modeled bridge exposure of $1.009bn, equal to $4.37 per share and 4.8% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Committed program funds or required operating liquidity included as excess cash would overstate the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: If we collect amounts in excess of amounts expended, we have a commitment to spend these amounts on the related programs.
audit_findings.explanation: Cash availability is unresolved, but the valuation adds only $1.009bn. Even removing the entire balance would reduce base value from $91.01 to about $86.64 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion; the actual adjustment cannot exceed the amount added.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the June cash balance to unrestricted corporate cash, program collections, operating liquidity and other unavailable amounts, and replace the bridge addition with verified excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Existing uncertain-tax claims may be missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $800m unrecognized tax benefits plus $232m related interest and penalties equals $1.032bn, or $4.47 per share and 4.9% of base equity value if fully incremental
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash settlement of previously expensed tax claims would reduce equity without necessarily reducing forecast OE when paid.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company recognized income tax expense of $611 million during the year ended December 31, 2025, and unrecognized tax benefits of $800 million as of December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The recorded balances are demonstrated, but the June carrying amount, settlement amount, timing, offsets and location within the valuation are not. The reported $1.032bn scale is near but below 5% of base equity value; actual exposure could differ materially from the accounting reserve, so materiality cannot be resolved from the record.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 2026 uncertain-tax and related-interest balances, expected settlement ranges and offsets; identify amounts already reflected in OE or other liabilities, then deduct and rerun only the incremental common-equity claim.

audit_findings.title: Hotel-owner guarantees create off-balance-sheet common-equity claims
audit_findings.magnitude: filed June 2026 maximum possible outlays of $56m for debt guarantees and loan commitments plus $13m for performance guarantees, totaling $69m or $0.30 per share and 0.3% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Expected guarantee losses should enter normalized OE, while an uncovered existing claim would reduce the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our debt guarantees and loan commitments as of December 31, 2025 had expirations ranging from 2027 to 2035 and remaining possible cash outlays totaling $ 61 million.
audit_findings.explanation: Past $77m payments demonstrate that losses can occur, but no current omission or expected loss is established. Even the latest disclosed maximum exposure of $69m is only 0.3% of base equity value, so it is not material to the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm June reserves and expected losses, include any normalized recurring loss in OE, and deduct only uncovered claims not already recognized.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: computed FY2024 residual of $60m from $146m filed D&A less $86m identified eligible D&A; FY2025 residual unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Eligible non-economic D&A left as an expense reduces OE and all scenario values.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2024 $86.0m (58.9% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: This is a deliberate conservative treatment, not a demonstrated error. The FY2024 residual was 4.2% of the current anchor as a scale comparison, but the record neither identifies the FY2025 residual nor proves that any residual represents an eligible add-back. Present materiality therefore cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the FY2025 D&A composition, classify each residual component against the OE add-back policy, and rerun only for amounts supported as non-economic and not offset by required reinvestment.
